+title: 'LSP stop and start: stop the language servers and start them again (engine)'
+---
+## What
+
+A host must be able to stop the language servers of a workspace and then start them again. A stopped server releases its file locks, thus a build cleanup (for example `swift package clean` or `rm -rf .build`) can run. The index, the watcher and the store continue to operate while the servers are stopped. The auto start and the auto install that `CodeContext.start()` does from project detection do not change.
+
+This card adds the engine API. The card for the `code_index` tool operations depends on this card.
+
+### The problem today
+
+- `LspSupervisor.shutdown()` (`Sources/FoundationModelsCodeContext/LSP/LspSupervisor.swift`) cancels the health loop task and the install task of each daemon, then shuts down each daemon. It keeps each entry in `managedDaemons` in the state `.notStarted`, with `healthLoopTask == nil`.
+- `LspSupervisor.start()` -> `performStart()` -> `spawnAndRegister(specs:)` skips each spec whose command is in `managedDaemons` (`specs.filter { managedDaemons[$0.command] == nil }`). Thus after `shutdown()`, a second `start()` starts no server.
+- `CodeContext` (`Sources/FoundationModelsCodeContext/CodeContext.swift`) calls `supervisor.shutdown()` only from `stop()`, which also stops the index loop, the LSP index tasks and the watcher. No public API stops only the servers.
+
+### The approach
+
+- [ ] In `LspSupervisor.spawnAndRegister(specs:)`, also spawn a spec whose entry is stopped. A stopped entry is an entry with `healthLoopTask == nil` (only `shutdown()` sets it to `nil`). Replace the stopped entry with the new daemon through `registerManagedDaemon(spec:daemon:)`, and cancel its old `installTask` first, as `insertDaemonForTesting(spec:daemon:)` does. Update the doc comments of `start()` and `shutdown()`: a `start()` after `shutdown()` starts the stopped servers again. The `inFlightStart` coalescing does not change.
+- [ ] Add `public func stopLanguageServers() async -> [ServerStatus]` to `CodeContext`. It calls `supervisor.shutdown()`, then `publishServersStatus()`, then gives `lspStatus()`. It does not cancel `lspIndexTasks`: `LSPIndexWorker.run` sleeps for `sessionUnavailableSleep` while `sessionProvider()` gives `nil`, and it continues when the servers start again. When the context is not started, the call does nothing and gives `lspStatus()`.
+- [ ] Add `public func startLanguageServers() async throws -> [ServerStatus]` to `CodeContext`. It calls `supervisor.start()` (a new project detection, thus a new project marker also gets its server, and a missing binary gets the auto install), then `publishServersStatus()`, then gives `lspStatus()`. When the context is not started, the call does nothing and gives `lspStatus()`. It rethrows the project detection errors of `LspSupervisor.start()`.
+- [ ] Write the doc comments in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English, in the style of the file.
+
+Files: `Sources/FoundationModelsCodeContext/LSP/LspSupervisor.swift`, `Sources/FoundationModelsCodeContext/CodeContext.swift`, `Tests/FoundationModelsCodeContextTests/LspSupervisorTests.swift`, `Tests/FoundationModelsCodeContextTests/CodeContextStartTests.swift`.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] After `LspSupervisor.shutdown()`, a call to `start()` (or to `startForTesting(specs:)`) starts each stopped daemon again: `status()` gives `.running(pid:)` for it, and its health loop task is not `nil`.
+- [ ] A `start()` while the daemons run does not spawn a second daemon for a command (the dedupe by command stays).
+- [ ] `CodeContext.stopLanguageServers()` gives each server in the state `.notStarted`, and `state.servers` shows the same states.
+- [ ] `CodeContext.startLanguageServers()` after `stopLanguageServers()` gives each server in a state that is not `.notStarted`.
+- [ ] Before `start()` and after `stop()` of the context, the two calls do nothing and give `lspStatus()`.
+- [ ] The existing tests of `LspSupervisorTests`, `CodeContextStartTests` and `LiveOpsExtendedTests` pass.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsCodeContextTests/LspSupervisorTests.swift`: add `startAfterShutdownStartsTheStoppedDaemonsAgain`. Use `startForTesting(specs: [Self.serverSpec(command: "true")])` with `fakeConnectionFactory`, expect `.running`, call `shutdown()`, expect `.notStarted`, call `startForTesting` again, expect `.running` again. Use `setDaemonConstructedHookForTesting` to count two daemon constructions.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsCodeContextTests/LspSupervisorTests.swift`: add `startWhileRunningDoesNotSpawnASecondDaemon`. Call `startForTesting` two times without `shutdown()`, and expect one daemon construction.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsCodeContextTests/CodeContextStartTests.swift`: add a test that `stopLanguageServers()` and `startLanguageServers()` before `start()` and after `stop()` give `lspStatus()` and throw no error. Add a test that after `start()`, `stopLanguageServers()` gives no server in a state other than `.notStarted`.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --filter "LspSupervisorTests|CodeContextStartTests|LiveOpsExtendedTests"`. All tests pass.
+- [ ] Run `swift test`. All tests pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #lsp #feature
